name: Bonita Casita

gallery.cap: Pool, spa and pool house from above
Outdoor shower, looking back to the main house

summary: The client for this pool house owns a home designed by the Dallas firm Far + Dang, whose partner Bang Dang taught Jason’s second-year design studio at UT Arlington.

The brief was a pool house that would feel respectful of, and cohesive with, the original architecture. The design began with a study of the existing entry, its scale and the rhythm of its window and door openings, so the new structure would sit naturally alongside the house.
scope: Design, permit set and construction documents

name: Courtshire

gallery.cap: Kitchen range wall and breakfast nook
Cutaway axonometric of the new plan

scope: Interior space planning, structural coordination, construction documents and millwork drawings
summary: This 1960s ranch house in North Dallas had a closed-off floor plan that the client wanted to open up. Three load-bearing walls were removed, and four new LVL beams were set into the attic to carry the roof load. The result is one continuous kitchen, living and dining area, with natural light and sight lines running from the front of the house to the back.

The details carry the same care. A quartzite-wrapped range hood anchors the kitchen. At the entry, a lit step resolves an existing change in level and marks the transition from the shared living spaces to the private bedroom wing. Custom pendant and sconce lighting completes the scheme.

steps.d: A 1960s ranch layout, with the kitchen, living and dining rooms closed off from one another.
Three load-bearing walls come out to join the kitchen, living and dining areas.
Four LVL beams, set into the attic, carry the roof load the walls used to support.
New cabinetry, built-ins and furniture fill the open plan.
One continuous space, with light and sight lines from the front of the house to the back.

details.d: A curved, lit step resolves an existing change in level and marks the move from the living areas to the bedroom wing.
A Flexitions stair nosing caps the step, with a corner-mount LED channel set beneath it to wash the 4-inch tile riser.
Custom-made sconces set against the arched openings between the kitchen and the butler’s pantry.

name: Mill Creek

gallery.cap: Open plan from the second-floor landing

sequence.title: How the second story was added

steps.d: The original single-story house, with the roof area to be removed outlined.
The roof over the center of the house lifts away, opening the plan below.
The new second story is set onto the existing walls below.

summary: With a baby on the way, the owners of this 1965 house needed more room for a growing family. The solution was a new second story built above the existing home, adding two bedrooms, a bathroom and a playroom.

Skylights and new windows bring natural light into the upper floor, with views over the backyard and the street. On the ground floor, the renovation opened up the plan, made the everyday spaces more functional and added a covered patio for entertaining.
scope: Design, permit set and construction documents

film.d: From the new second-floor playroom, down the stair to the open living, dining and kitchen.

name: Purdue Avenue

gallery.cap: Living room in the enclosed porch

scope: Design, construction documents and millwork drawings
summary: The family at this Preston Hollow home needed a larger living room and a better way into the house from the garage. Rather than build a full addition, the design enclosed the existing back porch, turning it into an extension of the living room and making space for a more functional kitchen.

A new mudroom connects the house to the existing garage, creating a seamless transition and a better arrival sequence into the home. Two new steel beams and several LVLs carry the existing second floor over the opened-up spaces below.

details.d: Cabinetry runs to the ceiling along the sink wall, with glass-front uppers, an apron-front sink under the window and a built-in banquette at the breakfast nook.

details.t: Range wall and living room built-ins
details.d: The range wall wraps around the corner beside a tall built-in refrigerator. Across the room, built-in shelving and cabinets frame the fireplace in the living room.

name: Winton Street

gallery.cap: Cutaway of the new second floor and stair

summary: This Dallas home needed more space without giving up any of the yard. The answer was to build up: a new second story set over the existing garage.

The existing covered patio between the house and the garage was enclosed and turned into the new stair hall, connecting the original ground floor to the rooms above. Space that sat mostly unused now does the work of joining old and new.
scope: Design, permit set and construction documents

gallery.cap: Framing, with a printed model of the house

name: Nuli Studios Med Spa
summary: Nuli Studios is a med spa brand with locations in Frisco and Southlake. For each suite of roughly 2,000 square feet, the studio prepared the permit set and construction documents that took interior designer Michele Pelafas's concept through permitting and into construction.
